dtc.priority: Run an AI-answer audit on each client's top 10 SKUs across ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google AI Mode this week. Shopify auto-activated Agentic Storefronts for all eligible US merchants on March 11, so AI engines are now stating brands' product facts directly in-chat and at checkout. The single highest-value action today is finding where those engines state wrong specs, prices or policies and fixing the first-party source data behind them — because under the Air Canada (2024) precedent the brand owns what its bot/agent says.

landscape.headline: Agentic Storefronts live by default for US merchants
landscape.body: Shopify auto-activated Agentic Storefronts for all eligible US merchants on March 11, 2026; 2M+ stores are now in ChatGPT product discovery. AI referral traffic to retail surged 693% YoY over the holiday period and converted 31% higher than non-AI sources (Adobe, 2026). What an AI states about a product is now a transaction surface, not a marketing one — wrong facts cost sales directly.

landscape.headline: Courts treating chatbots as 'products'; liability wave building
landscape.body: Following Air Canada (2024), courts are rejecting the 'the AI did it' defense and have begun treating chatbot outputs as products subject to liability (e.g. the Character.AI ruling). Gartner projects 2,000+ AI-related legal claims by end of 2026. A brand owns what its assistant/agent says about price, returns, allergens or compatibility.

landscape.headline: Google Merchant Center now reports brand presence in AI Mode
landscape.body: Google shipped a Merchant Center report tracking how a brand appears in AI Mode, and product-data quality has moved from a campaign-level variable to a surface-level one across AI Mode, AI Overviews and Gemini. A feed can pass all Merchant Center validation yet still be 'low completeness' for what AI shoppers actually ask — the gap is now measurable.

landscape.headline: AI Overviews spreading product/brand misinfo at scale
landscape.body: AI Overviews pull from forums, aggregators and outdated UGC when first-party entity signals are weak, surfacing wrong prices, specs and policies. Native 'report incorrect info' tools exist but corrections are slow and not guaranteed — the durable fix is strengthening the authoritative first-party sources the models cite.

Sold as a fixed-fee audit plus a monthly monitoring retainer. Frames on accuracy and liability, not 'getting recommended.'

cannabis.priority: Audit what AI assistants state about each cannabis client's THC/CBD content, health/medical claims, and the states where the brand is presented as available — then fix the source data and document it. The DEA's April 23 Schedule III order (FDA-approved + state-licensed medical only; recreational still Schedule I) plus the June 29 broader-rescheduling hearing mean AI is now confidently stating outdated legal status. The top action today is catching any AI output that implies wrong potency, a prohibited health claim, or availability in an unlicensed state — each is direct compliance liability for the brand.

landscape.headline: Schedule III order live; broader-rescheduling hearing June 29
landscape.body: Acting AG Blanche's April 23, 2026 order placed FDA-approved and state-licensed MEDICAL marijuana in Schedule III; recreational and anything outside those buckets remains Schedule I. An expedited DEA hearing on broader rescheduling runs June 29–July 15, 2026. AI assistants are already stating blanket 'cannabis is Schedule III now' — a wrong legal claim a brand can be tied to. Accuracy of legal-status statements is the live exposure.

landscape.headline: CA emergency rules: dual adult-use + medical licenses
landscape.body: On May 18 the DCC announced emergency regulatory action letting licensees hold separate adult-use and medical licenses simultaneously (effective ~June 5); ~1,600 California licensees are eligible. Dual-license holders must keep distinct books, Metrc track-and-trace accounts, insurance and permits. AI that conflates a brand's medical vs adult-use availability now risks misstating what's legally purchasable where.

landscape.headline: Health-claim class actions + no AI-vendor safe harbor
landscape.body: Health-risk class actions were filed May 4, 2026 against Cresco, Green Thumb, Verano and Curaleaf. Separately, 1,350+ AI hallucination cases are catalogued globally with no safe harbor based on a vendor's reputation. An AI stating an unsupported therapeutic benefit for a brand's product compounds existing health-claim liability.

landscape.headline: AI barely surfaces dispensaries — so this is accuracy, not visibility
landscape.body: A SOCi study of 350K+ locations found ChatGPT recommends only ~1.2% of dispensaries, Perplexity 7.4%, Gemini 11%, vs Google's local 3-pack at 35.9%, and AI surfacing is declining. The opportunity is not getting recommended — it's ensuring the rare times AI does mention a brand it states correct potency, legal status and availability.

Pairs the AI findings with a first-party source fix (site copy, COA/potency data, structured availability) and a documented remediation record the brand can show regulators. Framed as compliance-liability reduction, not visibility.
